H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H1961: to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary)
H4057: a pasture (i.e. open field, whither cattle are driven); by implication, a desert; also speech (including its organs)
H3063: Jehudah (or Judah), the name of five Israelites; also of the tribe descended from the first, and of its territory
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H410: strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity)
H859: thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you
H7836: properly, to dawn, i.e. (figuratively) be (up) early at any task (with the implication of earnestness); by extension, to search for (with painstaking)
H5315: properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental)
H1320: flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of aman
H776: the earth (at large, or partitively a land)
H1097: properly, failure, i.e. nothing or destruction; usually (with preposition) without, not yet, because not, as long as, etc.
H4325: water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen
H3651: properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles)
H6944: a sacred place or thing; rarely abstract, sanctity
H2372: to gaze at; mentally to perceive, contemplate (with pleasure); specifically, to have avision of
H7200: to see, literally or figuratively (in numerous applications, direct and implied, transitive, intransitive and causative)
H5797: strength in various applications (force, security, majesty, praise)
H3519: properly, weight, but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H2896: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
H2617: kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty
H2416: alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively
H8193: the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.)
H7623: properly, to address in aloud tone, i.e. (specifically) loud; figuratively, to pacify (as if by words)
H1288: to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason)
H8034: an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
H5375: to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
H3709: the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power
H3644: a form of the prefix 'k-', but used separately as, thus, so
H2459: fat, whether literally or figuratively; hence, the richest or choice part
H1880: the fat; abstractly fatness, i.e. (figuratively) abundance; specifically the (fatty) ashes of sacrifices
H7646: to sate, i.e. fill to satisfaction (literally or figuratively)
H1984: to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make ashow, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify
H6310: the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to
H518: used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not
H2142: properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention; to be male
H5921: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
H3326: spread, i.e. a bed; (architecture) an extension, i.e. wing or lean-to (a single story or collectively)
H1897: to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder
H3671: an edge or extremity; specifically (of a bird or army) a wing, (of a garment or bedclothing) a flap, (of the earth) a quarter, (of a building) a pinnacle
H7442: properly, to creak (or emit a stridulous sound), i.e. to shout (usually for joy)
H1692: properly, to impinge, i.e. cling or adhere; figuratively, to catch by pursuit
H310: properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses)
H8551: to sustain; by implication, to obtain, keep fast; figuratively, to help, follow close
H3225: the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south
H1245: to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after
H935: to go or come (in a wide variety of applications)
H8482: lowermost; as noun (feminine plural) the depths (figuratively, a pit, the womb)
H5064: to flow; figuratively, to stretch out; causatively, to pour out or down; figuratively, to deliver over
H3027: a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.),
H2719: drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement
H4521: an allotment (by courtesy, law or providence)
H8055: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H7650: to seven oneself, i.e. swear (as if by repeating a declaration seven times)
H5534: to shut up; by implication, to surrender
H1696: perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue
H8267: an untruth; by implication, a sham (often adverbial)
